implementation.name: original-v1-block-sparse-gemm
implementation.scope: Source pattern: a 3 × 3 grid of tiles, each dense tile 3 × 3; six stored tiles at (0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,2),(2,1),(2,2). Supporting numeric case: every stored scalar weight is 1; the activation column contains 1–9. Colors in the original do not encode these toy values.
implementation.question: How do block coordinates select reads and retain output sums?

purpose: Use each exact-pattern coordinate entry to select a dense activation block and update the correct retained output tile. Empty coordinates schedule no block multiplication.
storyboard: The verified original SVG is the primary diagram: blue dense 3 × 3 tiles in the sparse grid, packed nonzero mini-matrices and adjacent coordinate index, plus tall input/output matrices. Overlays retain partial sums in the first output column and target contribution motion to actual packed-tile/vector objects. A magnified 3 × 3 by 3 × 1 operation is a view of those same objects, not another allocation. Other columns are schematic context. Use each exact-pattern coordinate entry to select a dense activation block and update the correct retained output tile. Empty coordinates schedule no block multiplication.
guard: The 3 × 3 tile size matches the source; toy weights are explicitly separate from source colors. No Tensor Core, alignment, bandwidth, or speedup assertion.
